dogecoin.text: @dogecoin_empire I have no issue being with a woman who is financially more successful than myself.
@dogecoin_empire The confidence is sexy but I would be the one to propose in the end.
@dogecoin_empire This is correct. I appreciate women with natural beauty and I support any woman in their decision to not wear makeup.
@dogecoin_empire No, not at all. If a woman showed up at my house without makeup on for a first date, she would automatically be the one that I ask for on a second date.
@dogecoin_empire A woman who judges a man based solely on innate characteristics instead of his character should be avoided. That is enough for me.
@dogecoin_empire Not at all. I do not think it is an issue for women to want brawn and intelligence.

@dogecoin_empire I have yet to find a woman who wants to go out on a date to put it lightly. The main issue is that I tend to be critical of many women within the first fifteen minutes of interacting with them in person and I am working on this. The worst part is my intuition is 85-90% correct.

@dogecoin_empire I agree with parts of this post but I think the fundamental issue is that many young men and women struggle with having basic conversations. When men and women cannot relate with one another due to differences in culture, politics, or religion, relationships cannot begin.

@dogecoin_empire The concept of simply choosing a beautiful woman, from my perspective, is not solely about appearances. If a woman is honest, a great conversationalist, has a personality, she is kind and respectful, and she has a beautiful voice, these are my qualifies for a beautiful woman.
@dogecoin_empire Absolutely. That is why I avoid many single women romantically after 15 minutes of interacting with them in person.
@dogecoin_empire I have heard this from many single women, both online and in reality. The only irony is that I met many single women who want the opposite.
@dogecoin_empire There is a difference between genuine beauty and absolute narcissism. She is in the realm of narcissism.
